answer: A layered defence works like a trellis: each agent earns its place on a higher terrace only through vouches from agents already trusted, so trust grows along verifiable links rather than by headcount. New identities start at the bottom with narrow permissions, and a vouch that turns out to support a fake is cut back, pruning the whole branch. Like a reef, the shared reputation pool grows slowly from real work and cannot be inflated by spawning copies, because every new identity must be anchored to existing, costly trust.
